presentation.label: Headphones as a third output
presentation.summary: Turn the headphone jack into a third assignable output pair and pick each track's outputs with CUE + LEVEL.
presentation.overview: Adds ROUTED beside NORMAL and STUDIO in PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO (the box stock calls CUE CFG, titled ROUTING with the module). In ROUTED, LEVEL sets a track's level and CUE + LEVEL chooses where it plays: MAIN, CUE or PHONES as stereo pairs in any combination, or a single mono jack of the six (track L+R summed at half each, so a centred sound keeps its level). The choice is stored in the Part, so it survives SRC page resets, Part reload and project save. The MIXER's MIX knob becomes the PHONES output level. Inputs keep their stock DIR routing to MAIN.
highlights: Three stereo output pairs: MAIN, CUE and the headphone jack.
Per track: any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one mono jack (MAIN L/R, CUE L/R, PHONES L/R).
Routing lives in the Part: SRC page resets and track clears leave it alone.
With MASTER TRACK on, tracks routed to MAIN feed the master and track 8's destination picks where the master plays.
usage: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO: select ROUTING > ROUTED and press YES.
On a track, hold CUE: the LEV box shows the destination. Turn LEVEL to change it.
In the MIXER, MIX (labelled PHN) sets the PHONES output level. Choose NORMAL or STUDIO again to return to stock behaviour.

limitations: Builds with the stock DSP code built in (static_stock) and takes SPRING REV's program memory on core 0: SPRING REV leaves both effect menus while the module is installed.
The ROUTED mixdown costs core 0 up to about 216 more instructions per sample than stock (every track on ALL, MASTER on, bus levels moving); every track on MAIN adds about 20.
Switching to or from ROUTED rewrites every Part's LEVEL and cue bytes (and, into NORMAL, the project's cue settings) by documented rules; save to keep it.
A ROUTED project opened on a stock OS loads as STUDIO with tiny cue levels; switch to NORMAL or STUDIO before flashing another OS.
Changes core 0's mixdown and headphone crossfade; other modules that hook those sites are refused by the ledger.

resources.recorded: Measured in the ColdFire port (instructions) and from the build report

storage.label: Memory
storage.display: 1,498 B DRAM + 781 DSP P words + 193 DSP Y words
storage.conditions: ColdFire unit .text 1,272 B and .data 226 B (runtime ELF); DSP P code 739 words and a 42-word table in SPRING REV's harvested span on core 0; DSP Y $c00..$cc0. No per-track copies, no audio buffers.

processing.label: DSP core 0 mixdown
processing.conditions: Executed instructions of the mixdown (P:$257..$2d5) and headphone crossfade (P:$30a..$35a) per 16-sample frame, every track on ALL, MASTER on, MAIN/CUE/PHONES levels moving, including the frame that rebuilds the routing lists: 4,336 + 192 per frame. Stock: 880 + 191. Cycles and bus stalls are not modelled.

impact.conditions: Eight tracks in ROUTED at the dearest routing (every track on ALL, MASTER on, levels moving); NORMAL and STUDIO run stock code plus a 4-instruction check.

cpu.rationale: The level-page detour runs once a frame, 189 instructions typical and 229 at most (all eight tracks changing destination). The mode conversion runs once per switch in the UI task.

dsp.rationale: Up to about 216 extra instructions per sample on core 0 (about 7% of 3,120); about 20 with every track on MAIN.

memory.rationale: 1,498 bytes of DRAM code and data, 781 DSP program words reused from SPRING REV and 193 DSP Y words.

tests.summary: The image gate passes 76 checks under the ColdFire port: every destination, mono sums, MAIN against stock, the level law, MKII, MASTER, mute, DIR, the declick, every mode-conversion rule by the keys and a power cycle. On an MKII the author tested routing, levels, the MIXER, everyday flows, saving and power and the conversion (functional report, 7-8 Oct 2026). No timed stress run, no chip timing.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every destination code 0..13 per track, all eight tracks on ALL, mixed stereo and mono routings, MAIN/CUE/PHONES levels 0..127, MASTER on and off.
conditions.parameterModulation: MAIN, CUE and MIX levels changed every other frame for 60 frames; LEVEL, XVOL scenes, locks and LFOs act through stock gain ramps the mixdown reads, unchanged.
conditions.modeSwitching: All eight tracks changing destination in one frame (list rebuild and declick), and NORMAL/STUDIO/ROUTED switches.
conditions.maxLoad: One instance per unit (a global mode). Worst measured: 4,336 + 192 executed instructions per 16-sample frame on core 0, every track on ALL with MASTER on; stock 880 + 191.
conditions.inputConditions: Tone and four-input test audio; the code path does not depend on sample values. Counts are executed instructions, not modelled cycles.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every destination per track, levels 0..127, MASTER on and off.
conditions.parameterModulation: Level changes every other frame; not routed through LFOs or locks.
conditions.modeSwitching: All eight tracks changing destination in one frame (the declick path for each).
conditions.maxLoad: The level-page detour, once a frame: 189 executed instructions typical, 229 at most. Budget: 10% of a 362.8 us frame at 266 MHz. The mode conversion (16 banks x 8 Parts) runs once per switch in the UI task, outside the frame.
conditions.inputConditions: Independent of audio. Executed instructions; cycles and cache effects are not modelled.

regions.name: ColdFire data: tables, names, routing state (DRAM unit .data)
DSP core 0 program: mixdown and phones hooks, in SPRING REV's harvested span
DSP core 0 program: the 42-word destination table
DSP core 0 Y: bus factors, lists, PHONES buffer ($c00..$cc0)

memory.conditions: From the static build's runtime ELF and the DSP placement report. Detours patch stock instructions in place; the level-page words and battery-RAM copies the module uses are stock's. No heap; ColdFire stack use is the callers' frames plus at most 48 bytes (set_mode's saved registers and the conversion's call chain).

hardware.summary: On an Octatrack MKII the author flashed PHNSTAT8 and PHNSTAT9 (this source, stock DSP code built in, SPRING REV off the menus) and checked: tracks reach MAIN, CUE and PHONES separately, mono jacks and sides, LEVEL on every output, the MIXER's MAIN, CUE and PHN, the headphone knob, no zipper noise, a semi-busy project with tracks on PHONES without dropouts, mute and solo, page resets, Parts and Part reload, patterns, XVOL, metronome, inputs, the master track, save and power cycle with unsaved routing, project reload, the stock NORMAL and STUDIO flows, and ROUTED to STUDIO and NORMAL and back.
limitations: A functional interactive report, not a timed stress run; no audio or timing measurement on the chip.
Conversions in Parts other than the current one and in other banks were checked in the emulator only.
No combination with other modules on the unit.
Images with octabam's default stock-effect loader froze the unit (no sound, sequencer on trig 1) with or without this module; this module was tested only in static builds.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Press PROJ, open CONTROL > AUDIO, move right into ROUTING, select ROUTED and press YES.
Select track 1, hold CUE and turn LEVEL until the LEV box reads PHN: track 1 now plays only in the headphones.
Open the MIXER and turn MIX (PHN) to set the headphone level; choose NORMAL again to return to stock routing.

steps: Include Phones Routing in your build.
Press PROJ (MKII), open CONTROL > AUDIO, move right into the ROUTING box, select ROUTED and press YES.
Select an audio track, hold CUE and turn LEVEL to pick its outputs; the LEV box shows the destination.
Open the MIXER: MIX, labelled PHN, sets the headphone output level.
